ambiguities.statement: Authoritative map, does not override detail, and routing relationships only leave conflict precedence unclear when the index summary and an owner document disagree.
No open questions and deterministic defaults coexist with explicitly open blockers, deferred families, future reverification, and route-specific readiness.
Registered, strict, production, fully materializes, partial closure, and closes only are status terms with different proof strengths but no machine-visible status taxonomy in this window.
buildability_gate_passed remains false is expressed as a validator rule and current state without a named transition authority or temporal scope for eventually changing it.
The required reading order is scoped to orchestrator rewrite canon-collapse but can appear globally mandatory, while many newly registered critical owner and readiness documents are absent.
Current toolchain and provider assertions do not identify a freshness receipt, expiry threshold, or deterministic response when official live truth differs.
deferred_not_build_blocking classification includes consequential permission and runtime-facing families, but its risk threshold and authority are not stated here.
Primary owner, primary doc, cross-owner, strongly implicated, adjacent owner, stale consumer, already implicated, and impacted_docs labels have no defined obligation or lifecycle differences.

builder_discretion.statement: Builders determine when live Plans and allowed indexes are stable enough for an explicit governance seal.
Implementers determine how and when to reverify Rust/Slint releases and what to do if official stable versions differ.
Provider readiness remains route/model/account-specific without a decision algorithm in this map.
Whole-MVP container runtime families are capability-probed and gated without a stated minimum capability set or degradation policy.
Owners define reasons and reopen conditions for deferred storage families, including permissions and browser/worktree state.
Reconciliation participants determine what counts as stale tier-era, request-era, or mixed-era canon and when owner/consumer reconciliation is complete.
Live provider projection sync is deferred to a separate lane whose trigger, permission boundary, and failure policy are unspecified here.

candidate_findings.finding: No open questions and deterministic defaults may falsely signal semantic closure despite explicit lifecycle, harness, security, persistence, GUI, currentness, and provider blockers.

Buildability gating lacks an atomic, fail-closed currentness contract across blocker, gate, and node-readiness artifacts, while buildability_gate_passed is required to remain false without an explicit future transition protocol.
The trusted local daemon for browser-hosted GUI access to OS capabilities is a consequential security boundary with no stated authentication, origin, authorization, or compromise model.
Static provider and Rust/Slint currentness assertions lack receipts, expiry, migration, and deterministic mismatch handling.

Production, fully materialized, and closed security/behavioral labels can be flattened into implementation readiness even though the evidence is explicitly non-executable and permission/runtime families remain deferred.
The anti-drift reading order and owner-first rules lack a reconciliation oracle and omit many later-registered critical owners, allowing stale consumers to appear compliant.
The change summary is not chronologically ordered and its ContractRef declarations do not clearly encode all authorities introduced, creating currentness and traversal risk.
Cross-doc seam classifications and the impacted_docs seam lack defined obligations, ownership, transition-to-reconciled state, and acceptance evidence.

claims.claim: The index presents itself as an authoritative navigation and canonicalization map that follows DRY and deterministic decision policy, but does not override owner-plan detail or re-own subsystem behavior.

The change summary registers owner routing, lineage retirements, strict schemas, validators, production-named artifacts, and repeated non-executable boundaries across planning, providers, GUI, containers, and runtime contracts.

Provider, GUI/toolchain, and model-capability authority is currentness-sensitive: routes are model/account-specific, Rust/Slint versions require live reverification, and Models_System owns active capability provenance while Contracts V0 carries only snapshot references.

Implementation-readiness registries, matrices, reports, and scripts gate buildability; Approve And Build remains disabled while blockers are open or PNC-019 remains hard-disabled, and structural or validator evidence is explicitly insufficient.

Execution context, EventRecord, and storage-value schemas register versioned ownership and partial persistence materialization, while numerous runtime, security, GUI, provider, permission, and lifecycle blockers remain open or deferred.

Non-executable closure evidence closes only spec/schema/validator/fixture scope, leaves runtime lifecycle and clean-room harness open, keeps PNC-019 disabled and buildability false, and authorizes no runtime or product work.

Web operation schemas, no-secret projection artifacts, lineage receipts, fixtures, and coverage maps register broad policy and contract shapes, but generated governance refresh, live provider sync, and executable implementation remain separate lanes.
Legacy platform_specs authority is retired; Models_System owns context, token, fallback, provenance, and requested/effective capability fields.
A fixed ten-document owner-first reading order precedes primary consumers, and mirrors are reconciled only after owners and consumers.

The cross-doc guard classifies primary owners, adjacent consumers, stale consumers, and impacted docs for contract, storage, UI, usage, run-graph, HITL, executor, and artifact seams without transferring behavioral ownership to the index.

cross_window_seams.statement: Core authority and navigation disclaimers are completed by the context guard stating that the index records routing only and owner entries retain behavioral canon.
The Cross-doc owner-map guard heading begins in the core and its operative routing taxonomy occupies the authorized following context.
The capsule declares no previous window and names WIN-00-plans-index-0002 as next; that window was not inspected.

invalid_reason: Substantive reviewer agent identities were reused across successive window/role assignments, violating the Fresh Agent Isolation Protocol.

negative_space_observations.statement: No fail-closed behavior, atomic snapshot identity, staleness rule, or TOCTOU protection is stated for the blocker registry, gate matrix/report, node-readiness report, and approval decision.
The trusted local daemon boundary lacks stated authentication, origin binding, capability scoping, revocation, transport, local-network exposure, CSRF, or compromised-browser behavior.
Provider retirement and replacement lack stated migration, rollback, unavailable-provider, in-flight-operation, credential-transfer, or account-conflict behavior.
Schema registrations expose versions but this window gives no unknown-version, downgrade, replay-idempotency, concurrent-writer, partial-migration, or corrupt-record behavior.

Permission, browser, terminal, worktree, project-state, provider, and GUI storage families are deferred as non-build-blocking without adversarial criteria showing when their absence becomes security- or launch-critical.

Web schemas and negative fixtures cover permission, cache, egress, timeout, unavailable-browser, and citation cases, but no executable enforcement, malicious-content containment, SSRF boundary, runtime redaction, or failed-sync rollback is established here.
Owner-first reconciliation has no completion oracle, conflict adjudicator, version receipt, stale-term detector, or atomic update rule across owners, consumers, summaries, and checklists.
Governance-seal and generated-artifact registrations lack stated cancel, retry, resume, rollback, or partial-write behavior when a refresh fails.
